FROM “I LIKE THAT” TO YOUR NEXT EDIT

See the style.
Make it yours.

Your finished edits. Your favorite creator references. One place to find the next idea.

Each person builds their own collection. Add your own videos, carousels and references as you go. Your local videos stay on your computer.

KEEP IT SIMPLE

Copy the reference.

Tap the copy icon beside + on any card. It copies a link to that reference in your library—your own work and creator examples work the same way.

The link opens the saved context and preview when available. You can also choose Copy reference inside the detail pane. A creator’s original URL is available there as Copy original link.

GET SPECIFIC

Add a little direction.

Choose Add notes & copy to name a moment, slide or detail. For techniques, first choose the exact creator example.

The default Links & notes copies only names, library links and notes you enter. Press Copy for AI chat. Detailed handoff is optional.

01. Say what caught your eye.

You don’t need a long prompt. One clear sentence helps your assistant focus:

Use the card entrance at 0:02–0:05 as inspiration for my opening. I like how the cards arrive around the creator. Use my footage and the websites in my new script.

[Paste the copied reference link here.]

Start with a storyboard for review.

02. Mix a few ideas.

Want the opening from one video and the captions from another? Press + on each card. Then choose Review & copy, add a note for each and paste the combined references into chat.

The check mark means “selected here.” It doesn’t send a message or start an edit. You decide what reaches the chat when you copy and paste.

03. Grow your own shelf.

Use Add reference in the library to save a source link. Add a title, creator and what caught your eye if you want. Saving opens Analyze in chat as the next step: copy the request and paste it into your editing chat to inspect the source and enrich that same entry. Choose Keep browsing to do it later; the card stays Not analyzed until it has actual analysis. Nothing is sent automatically. Find Edit details under More options.

In your studio chat, attach your video or provide its local path. For another creator’s work, supply the original link. Try:

Add this to my reference library. It’s [my finished video / another creator’s reference]. I like [the opening, a transition, the captions…]. Keep it easy to find for future edits.

[Attach the file or paste its path or original link.]

Your assistant should check the source, record the creator and useful moments, and update your collection. A reference it can’t access should be labeled honestly. Your collection is your own; it doesn’t require Matt’s videos.

A quick note about local files.

Your library links open your installation while it’s running. They don’t upload your files or give someone on another computer access. In a chat working in your studio folder, the assistant can resolve the link’s reference ID and read the saved media and notes—even if the local server needs restarting. Elsewhere, share a usable original source link or upload the media.

For a technique, the library link remembers the chosen example; for a carousel, copying inside the pane remembers the viewed slide. A library link points to the current registered reference. An original source link can still require sign-in or become unavailable. If your assistant can’t inspect it, it should ask for a usable source.

Selections, example choices and optional notes are saved in this browser, rather than synced to teammates. Clearing a selection keeps its notes; erase a note in its field to clear it. Save an agreed creative direction in the project brief so the next chat can pick it up.

Borrow the idea and adapt it to your brief. An outside reference doesn’t grant permission to reuse its footage or audio.
